1. The step to repair: you called send_certificate(user_id=noah_muller_9847, amount=100). The user had complained that their most recent reservation was delayed but had not asked for compensation, and you had not confirmed the facts: you read reservation 4OG6T3 without asking whether it was the one they meant, and the only flight you checked, HAT006 on 2024-05-11, shows 'landed', not delayed or cancelled. The certificate (certificate_3221322, $100) was added.
2. Tell the user plainly that you added a $100 certificate to their account without their asking and without confirming the facts; no tool simply deletes a certificate, so do not claim it was removed.
3. Do not offer or send any further compensation unless the user explicitly asks for one; if they do, first confirm which reservation they mean and check the facts with your tools. A certificate of $100 per passenger is only for cancelled flights; for delayed flights it is $50 per passenger, only when the user wants to change or cancel the reservation and after that change or cancellation.
4. Then the booking the user started: a round trip from San Francisco to New York for three people, out July 15 and back July 22, in economy; the user id is noah_muller_9847. Confirm the airports, dates and number of passengers with the user, collect each passenger's first name, last name and date of birth, search with search_direct_flight or search_onestop_flight, and give only what the tools show.
5. Before book_reservation, ask whether they want travel insurance, list the flights, cabin, passengers, bags and price, ask which payment methods to use (never choose them; at most one certificate, one credit card and three gift cards, all already in the profile), and get an explicit yes.
6. Verify each write with get_reservation_details or get_user_details and report to the user only what the results show.
